context: You repaired a refuge, made a bed, and brought the stranded crew inside. You later assembled a lit shared workbench and took a supper portrait together.

scenario.title: Mars: A Light That Answers
scenario.premise: A damaged landing strands a small expedition. Recovery becomes a rescue, then a return journey carrying people and evidence. This is an engineering story with recovered qualified systems, not real survival instructions.

stage.title: The long night
stage.speaker: Camp engineer
stage.motivation: The refuge we repaired kept the recovered crew safe, but its exposed service wall loses heat overnight. Compare the wall samples in the chamber, then fit a screen to the same refuge so everyone can sleep comfortably.
stage.travelText: We return to the refuge where we sheltered the crew. Its exposed service wall is losing heat; the camp’s thermal chamber and screen kit are nearby.

areas.label: What the cliff can tell us

things.label: Provisioned refuge
things.description: The crew are sheltered, warm and fed. Their recovered equipment remains here for the next part of the expedition.

things.label: Lit workbench
things.description: The portable expedition workbench we assembled at camp, with its lamp still fitted. Its stiff mounting rails accept the guarded bench-top machine’s integral clamps.

things.label: Crew message
things.description: A personal recording from the rescued crew, not a report card or abstract morale resource.

things.label: Long range radio
things.description: Fit the directional antenna to the existing radio.

things.label: Message home
things.description: The crew’s recorded message sent home; a tangible recording of reaching other people again.

things.label: Wall sample
things.description: A spare piece of the recovered refuge’s wall assembly, supplied for the camp thermal chamber.

things.label: Temperature logger
things.description: A ready temperature recorder that can capture a cooling trace.

things.label: Thermal blanket
things.description: A mission insulating blanket that can be fitted to the measured wall dimensions.

things.label: Clip frame
things.description: The rigid reusable frame for the cabin’s removable thermal screen.

things.label: Measured wall template
things.description: The existing full-size outline of the refuge’s removable service-wall screen, with its fixing points marked.

things.label: Insulation swatch
things.description: A spare test swatch of the mission blanket material, kept with the wall coupon.

locations.label: Thermal chamber
locations.description: The camp’s enclosed qualification chamber provides a controlled cooling cycle for the wall sample; exposed outdoor readings would mix changing wind and sunlight.

cacheNarrative.label: Camp thermal workshop stores
cacheNarrative.narrative: The camp’s service cabinet holds the refuge wall sample, its measured template and the removable screen kit. The refuge and its prepared bed are the ones we already restored.
